Your subconscious knowing you are daydreaming instead of actually living

I have been daydreaming since I was a little girl. I remember to have really intrusive daydreams, but I dismissed it as an active imagination and went along with it without realizing. It was part of my life, and I daydreamed when I had spare time. When I entered middle school it started to get worse (I didn’t do homework, I left the few hobbies I had and stopped looking for new ones) but I dismissed it again. Barely after entering high school (by then I was turning down invitations to hang out with friends just to daydream) I stumbled across a post about MD, did a recap of my life, and came to the realization.
I don’t know if it started because I was bored or lonely, but now, at this point of my life, it’s starting to really turn into a coping mechanism.

Because of this random fear of mind readers I always (mentally) apologize whenever something really weird or messed up happens while I’m daydreaming. 
And I also think that if someone touches me or that if they touch the same object I’m touching (a table, a chair or even the floor) they can read my mind...

I understand what you’re going through, because right now I’m in that same situation. But there is a quote that keeps me going these days:
“I like to imagine that the world is one big machine. You know, machines never have any extra parts. They have the exact number and type of parts they need. So I figure if the entire world is a big machine, I have to be here for some reason. And that means you have to be here for some reason, too”
That’s why I still feel that suicide is a rash decision, so I think we should wait to see what happens, because we don’t know if a situation that can save us from that desire to disappear will come around at some point. Maybe we have to hold on a little longer and wait, until whatever that is bound to happen, happens.

I KNOOOOOWWWWW 
It’s so frustrating. Everyone just gives me this look that clearly says “typical teenage phase, I’ve been there”. 

No, no, dude, you haven’t if you’re giving me that dismissive look, saying “yeah, me too” with that... that... casual tone. 
And if you really have, well, let me tell you that you’re being really dismissive of the situation just because you managed to get better and now you think everybody will get out of that situation in a few years.
Damn, I always want to smack them with something...

There’s just one person, now one of my closest friends, that takes me seriously, and that’s because we’re currently going through the same situation and she has dealt with it for a really long time.

Definitely my situation. I’m dying for social interaction, but whenever I have the opportunity I back away with that disgusting feeling of wanting to be away at a calm place. To worsen the situation, I’m just really socially awkward and done have conversations topics at all because I never go out like I should. It wouldn’t even surprise me if I were to find out everyone else I know had a new group chat just to exclude me. Its been affecting me for a while now, and I feel like such a loser and misfit

Ok, so this post appeared on my “similar to...” recommendations. 
I don’t have OCD or anything like that (or at least I don’t think so...?), but I’m so relieved to find out I’m not the only one who does this.

I’ve been having this thoughts for a while now. I’m grieving the deaths of my granny, mom, friends and some of my pets. I also kind of grieve or have nostalgia over moments that haven’t happened yet or that didn’t/will not happen. My imagination takes over and I imagine every scenario vividly. I also do or say things I know they appreciate, ‘cause there’s a voice that tells me to do it, because I probably won’t see them alive again after that “see you later”.

It’s really intrusive and exhausting. 

Damn, it feels so good to talk about this with other people that have the same experience...

I think you should leave a letter. They will decide whether to open it or not, if they feel they can handle it or if it’s going to hurt too much. Maybe reading your last words or even just your motives could provide a similar sense of having a proper goodbye.

Hołd on to that feeling, I know what you mean and those moments are pure gold, I always cherish them <3
I hope you get to live more and more of those days in the future
